title: Surjectivity of the compatible component map
statement: Let R be a reduced Noetherian commutative ring and let compatible maps from its total fraction ring to all minimal-prime localizations be given. The induced component map is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02LX, finite product decomposition

proof.text: The localization prime correspondence IsLocalization.primeSpectrumOrderIso identifies Spec Q(R) with the primes of R disjoint from the nonzerodivisors. Ideal.iUnion_minimalPrimes and finite prime avoidance (Ideal.subset_union_prime) show that each such prime is minimal; conversely minimal primes avoid the nonzerodivisors. This gives fractionPrimeEquiv.

The contractions give an injection of Spec Q(R) into the finite set of minimal primes of R. Any inclusion between prime ideals of Q(R) contracts to an inclusion of minimal primes, hence an equality; the order embedding on ideals reflects equality. Extending each prime to a maximal ideal therefore shows that every prime of Q(R) is maximal. PrimeSpectrum.discreteTopology_iff_finite_and_krullDimLE_zero gives a discrete spectrum, including the empty-spectrum case.

For the prime of Q(R) corresponding to q_i, IsLocalization.isLocalization_isLocalization_atPrime_isLocalization and IsLocalization.algEquiv identify its localization with R_{q_i} as an R-algebra. The given component map followed by this equivalence equals the canonical localization map out of Q(R), by IsLocalization.ringHom_ext and compatibility on R.

PrimeSpectrum.toPiLocalization_bijective gives the canonical product decomposition for the discrete spectrum (all of whose primes are maximal). For injectivity, equality of the given components gives equality in every prime localization after applying the factor equivalences, so the canonical injective map gives equality. For surjectivity, transport a prescribed tuple to the prime-indexed localizations with Equiv.piCongrLeft, choose its preimage under the canonical surjective map, and use injectivity of each factor equivalence to recover the prescribed components. These are the two halves of the fully proved private lemma fraction_components_bijective.
Take the surjectivity component of fraction_components_bijective.

proof_origin.place: Stacks Tag 02LX, prime correspondence, finite discrete spectrum, and identification of the local factors; Tag 00EW for the zerodivisors. Formalized directly with Mathlib in P2.

lean.statement:
theorem fractionRing_pi_surjective_of_compatible
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsReduced R]
    {t : ℕ} {q : Fin t ≃ {p : PrimeSpectrum R // p.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes R}}
    (φ : ∀ i : Fin t, FractionRing R →+* Localization.AtPrime (q i).val.asIdeal)
    (hφ : ∀ i : Fin t, (φ i).comp (algebraMap R (FractionRing R)) =
      algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime (q i).val.asIdeal)) :
    Function.Surjective (RingHom.pi φ)
